summary: Summation No. 29 covers February 1948 (with most economic statistics for January or December). Politically it is dominated by the resignation of the Katayama Cabinet on 10 February after the Social Democratic left wing revolted over rail and postal rate rises in a supplementary budget, followed by a prolonged contest in which the Democratic leader Hitoshi Ashida was chosen prime minister over Liberal Shigeru Yoshida. The report also covers the hunt for hoarded goods, the National Diet Library Law, purge screening totals, police decentralization, war-crimes trials, and the prosecution's summation before the International Military Tribunal for the Far East. Economic sections give January output for coal, steel, textiles, power and transport, the 1947 foreign-trade totals, price controls, banking and liquidation figures, and reparations transfers. Social sections report nutrition surveys, the 1 October 1947 census (79.6 million), education conferences and media. Historians will find the Cabinet-crisis narrative and the quantitative series most useful.
highlights: The Katayama Cabinet resigned on 10 February after the Social Democratic left wing (Satake-hai) refused the supplementary budgets raising railway and postal rates; it had served eight months since 1 June 1947.

After weeks of interparty talks, Hitoshi Ashida of the Democratic Party was elected prime minister, winning 216 votes on the first ballot in the House of Representatives, though the Councillors had favored Yoshida; the Lower House choice prevailed.

Hoarded and concealed goods worth about 1,400,000,000 yen at official prices were uncovered between November and January; the Illegal Transactions Investigation Committee probed Diet members, and a comprehensive inventory of critical goods was ordered.
The National Diet Library Law passed both Houses unanimously on 4 February, creating a national library modeled on the Library of Congress following the 1947 United States Library Mission.

Purge screening had provisionally designated 202,413 persons by 21 February, of whom 173,602 were finally designated; 163 of 1,424 information-media officials screened were barred, and the Hirano court injunction was ruled void.

At the Tokyo war crimes trial the defense finished surrebuttal on 10 February and the prosecution began its summation on 11 February, with Chief Counsel Joseph Keenan's team charging 25 defendants under a 60-count indictment.
Japan's 1947 trade was about $526,000,000 imports and $175,000,000 exports, with roughly 92 percent of imports from the United States and foodstuffs 58 percent of import value.
The 1 October 1947 census counted 79,626,729 persons, about 5.6 percent above 1946; Bank of Japan notes outstanding stood at 215,219,000,000 yen on 29 February.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover of Summation No. 29 (February 1948), table of contents for Parts I-IV, and lists of charts, maps and tables numbered 1-113.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: no SCAP reorganization, Katayama resignation and Ashida election, economic output figures, and social developments including the October 1947 census.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: One-paragraph statement that the non-military organization of GHQ SCAP did not change during February 1948.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Cabinet resignation of 10 February, Ashida's election, hoarded-goods drive, National Diet Library Law, purge screening totals (202,413 designated provisionally), police decentralization and war-crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Summary of January output in agriculture, mining, industry, textiles, transport and communications, plus 1947 trade totals, finance, antitrust (267 concerns designated), reparations and science.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Nutrition surveys, venereal disease campaign, 79,626,729 census total, education conferences, Christian conferences, newspaper survey (2,978 papers) and cultural items.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Detailed account of the Katayama Cabinet crisis and Ashida's election, hoarded goods, Diet and purge, crime and police statistics, and war crimes trials including the IMTFE prosecution summation.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Katayama Cabinet falls 10 February over rate increases; Ashida elected prime minister with 216 votes; hoarded-goods inquiries; party maneuvers; Diet Library Law; purge screening of 671,120 persons.

sections.title: Cabinet Crisis
sections.summary: Social Democratic left wing opposes the rate-increase budget bills; Cabinet decides 7 February to hand the issue to the Diet; party leaders' statements and Katayama's 10 February resignation statement.

sections.title: Record of the Katayama Cabinet
sections.summary: Review of the cabinet's eight months: Ministry of Labor created, Home Ministry dissolved, eight-point economic program, anti-hoarding drive and the Law for Decentralization of Excessive Concentrations.

sections.title: Election of New Prime Minister
sections.summary: Interparty conferences from 10 February, Democratic and Social Democratic policy programs, Ashida elected in the Lower House, Yoshida in the Upper House, joint committee deadlock.

sections.title: Hoarded Goods
sections.summary: 1.4 billion yen of hidden goods found November-January, Economic Stabilization Board finds worth 100,000,000 yen, weapons seized at Kawasaki, and Diet committee probes including the Hara and Kondo cases.

sections.title: Political Parties and the Diet
sections.summary: Party positions during the crisis, National Diet Library Law of 4 February, dissolution of the Central Liaison Office, Upper House by-elections won by Liberals, and 26 February fire at purge records building.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: December crime and arrests, autonomous police in 1,604 of 1,808 municipalities, prison population of 82,760 in January, 943 railway accidents, and December fire losses.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Office of Attorney General begins 15 February; Class B and C trial results; IMTFE surrebuttal ends 10 February and the prosecution's summation begins 11 February.

sections.title: Legal Affairs and National War Crimes Trials
sections.summary: Attorney General office, 85 investigations completed, 40 persons ordered apprehended, and 19 trials of 48 accused including death sentences for Ishizaki and Katsudo.

sections.title: International Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: Court sessions in February, defense surrebuttal for Hirota and Taku, and the prosecution's summation on conspiracy, Manchuria, Southwest Pacific and aggression against the USSR.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: January and February economic reporting: farm land sales, coal, metals and chemicals, manufacturing, textiles, transport, communications, labor, trade, prices, finance, property control and science.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Government land sales of 32,700 cho in January, purchases of 94,655 cho on 2 February, livestock population changes and fish landings.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Whaling catch of 271 blue whale units, January log production of 57,107,500 cubic feet, coal output of 2,829,200 tons, stockpiles of 667,200 tons and crude oil production.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke, iron and steel, light and nonferrous metals, rubber, construction, shipbuilding, chemicals and machinery; January output hit by power shortages and New Year holidays.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: January flour and food processing, pulp (down 2,230 tons), glass, optical, electrical goods, motor vehicles, rubber goods, leather (758,200 pounds), agricultural equipment and miscellaneous goods.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: Cotton recovering from low levels, raw silk at its lowest in a year, rayon staple at lowest since May 1947, wool limited by fiber shortage.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: 108,231 motor vehicles registered, 291,629,562 railway passengers, 1,480,747 tons shipping cargo, electric generation of 2,233,000,000 kWh and gas production.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: Radiotelephone extended to Canada, Cuba and Mexico, radiotelegraph rates to U.S. revised, postal services, equipment production and December Ministry of Communications deficit of 1,208,818,199 yen.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Labor ministry ordinance of 7 February on illegal labor supply, anti-Communist union drives, no major strikes, union education programs, wages and employment security.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Calendar 1947 trade: about $526,000,000 imports and $175,000,000 exports, trade deficit, patterns by country and commodity, with 92 percent of imports from the United States.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Staple-food rations met in full, sugar incentive plan liberalized 19 February, price changes for explosives, rolling stock and cement, Tokyo water rates and urban family expenditures.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes at 215,219,000,000 yen, Reconstruction Finance Bank loans, securities liquidation, tax receipts, supplementary budgets approved 24 February and national debt.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: 943 looted ships recorded, restricted concerns, 267 industrial firms designated excessive concentrations, antitrust orders and 3,850 packages (7,294 tons) of advance reparations shipments.

sections.title: Section 13. Science and Technology
sections.summary: Science council's sixth meeting 30-31 January, 31 Japanese Standards promulgated, 103 patents granted, scientific organizations and Kyushu University research publications.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health, nutrition, population, welfare, education, religion, cultural resources and information media for February 1948.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Nutrition surveys, venereal disease campaign, medical supply production, narcotics, public assistance, Red Cross, repatriation and vital statistics including the 1947 census.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion, Cultural Resources and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Teacher conferences, textbook printing of 147,214,307 copies authorized, Christian conferences, first postwar art exchange, press, radio and film reports, and map of Japan.
